title: Transfer news LIVE: Villa set to complete Manzambi hijack, Inter to return for Jones as Liverpool reject bid, Trossard nears Besiktas move | talkSPORT
text:
The World Cup may well be taking centre stage this summer, but the new Premier League season will be upon us before we know it.

And the rumour mill never stops churning as top-flight sides eye deals before the 2026/27 campaign gets going.

Follow our live blog below for all the latest news, done deals and speculation from around the Premier League and beyond...

Unfortunately, no EFL round-up with Jamie O'Hara this season on The Sports Bar after Tottenham Hotspur avoided relegation.

But there is plenty of transfer activity in England's second and third tiers.

Former Premier League champions Leicester City are preparing for life in League One with the signing of Conor Chaplin.

John Percy is reporting that the forward is having a medical ahead of joining on a free transfer.

And Southampton have agreed a fee for Lewis Dobbin.

The Saints are set to pay Aston Villa £9million to bring the striker to the south coast.

Newcastle United must feel like they are in that film Groundhog Day because they've been hijacked again!

The Magpies agreed a fee with Freiburg last week for Johan Manzambi, who shone for Switzerland at the World Cup.

At that point, they were told the player wanted to wait until after Switzerland were out to make a decision.

Personal terms were verbally agreed, but the player had never actually said yes.

talkSPORT understands they always feared a hijack, and it is the self-fulfiling prophecy because the club and its fans were so worried about it that they almost manifested it.

Aston Villa have swooped in and offered Manzambi Champions League football.

He is now set to sign a long-term contract at Villa Park, and there is even footage that has emerged showing the player telling Emi Martinez he was joining Villa.

For Newcastle, it's another brutal blow after missing out on Victor Munoz and several other players over the last 12 months.

Actor and West Ham fan Danny Dyer has confirmed to talkSPORT that he thinks Jarrod Bowen will be staying with the Irons this summer.

The winger missed out on selection for the England squad and is set for at least a season in the Championship if he stays.

He is married to Danny's daughter, Dani, and is loved by Hammers fans.

Speaking to Ian Abrahams, or The Moose, Dyer said: "He's a very great, loyal man.

"First and foremost, he is my family, the father of my grandchildren, of course. It's been tough for him.

"He does deserve Champions League football and whatever decision he makes, or made, I would have supported him.

"I don't think he's going anywhere, and I think he will rip up the Championship, don't you worry yourself about that."

Besiktas are now very close to an agreement with Leandro Trossard on personal terms, talkSPORT understands.

Advanced talks are ongoing between the parties, with the Turkish giants confident of getting a deal done.

A fee of £17million has already been agreed with Arsenal.

The Belgium international is expected to join on a three-year contract with an option for a further year.

Inter Milan are set to bid again for Curtis Jones despite seeing a £21.2million approach instantly rejected.

Liverpool are prepared to keep Jones if their valuation isn’t met, with them understood to be wanting north of £30m.

Inter’s last verbal approach had led the Reds to conclude a deal for their homegrown midfielder wasn’t possible.

However, the Serie A side are now working on a new proposal, although no negotiations are currently ongoing.

Jones has not agreed terms with fellow Premier League side Nottingham Forest despite some reports.

Well, Newcastle could feel it coming and it's happened...

They were wary of a hijack of their deal for Johan Manzambi, as the player hadn't given the green light just yet.

A £51million fee had been agreed with Freiburg, but Aston Villa were understood to be potential challengers.

And now, Villa appear to have pulled off a hijack.

talkSPORT understands that they are in the process of finalising a move to sign Manzambi, who wants to join the club.

The 20-year-old midfielder is set to sign for Unai Emery's side, with Newcastle's lack of confidence in the deal proving correct.

It means the Magpies are going to miss out on yet another transfer target at the last minute, having been hijacked by Liverpool for Victor Munoz already this summer.

Newcastle are having to wait on the approval of Johan Manzambi before they can get their £51m deal over the line.

And that leaves the door open for a potential hijack...but in the meantime, the Magpies have secured another signing.

According to transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano, they have agreed to sign Kyran Thompson from Arsenal's academy.

The winger is an England U17 international and he became a free agent this summer after his Gunners deal expired.

Thompson had five proposals, but he's decided to join Newcastle and work under Eddie Howe.

The exodus at Newcastle looks set to continue as Everton are keen on winger Jacob Murphy, talkSPORT understands.

After nine years at St James' Park, the 31-year-old is being considered by the Toffees, who are aiming to strengthen on the wing.

Newcastle were looking to sign Victor Munoz before Liverpool hijacked that transfer.

They have, however, landed Ivory Coast World Cup star Bazoumana Toure for £40million.

And with just 12 months left on Murphy's contract in the North East, a move to Everton may well suit all parties.

Alex Jimenez will undergo a medical at Fiorentina ahead of a loan move from Bournemouth, talkSPORT understands.

The deal includes an option to sign the defender permanently for €20million (£17m) with bonuses, as well as a 30 per cent sell-on clause.

Jimenez is currently the subject of an external investigation, which is still ongoing, after posts which appear to show him exchanging inappropriate messages with an underage girl emerged on social media.

Whilst this is in place, the Spaniard cannot play in the UK and is currently suspended.

This move suits all parties and allows Jimenez to continue playing whilst still being on Bournemouth's books.

The 21-year-old made 32 appearances for the Cherries last season, initially joining on loan from Milan, before the move was made permanent in February for a £16.5million fee.

Coventry have announced the signing of winger Loum Tchaouna from Burnley on a five-year contract.

The 22-year-old becomes Frank Lampard's first fresh signing of the summer transfer window, as he joins for an undisclosed fee.

Frank Onyeka was the Sky Blues' first official arrival, whose loan move was made permanent in line with the obligation to buy subject to the team's promotion from the Championship.

And now the Premier League new boys have stepped up their business by snapping up Tchaouna, who will now remain a top-flight player despite suffering relegation with Burnley last term.

The France Under-21 international leaves Turf Moor after just a year, having joined the Clarets from Lazio in the summer of 2025.

Tchaouna made 32 appearances and scored three times in all competitions for Burnley during the 2025/26 campaign.

Upon joining Coventry, he told the club: “I’m so excited to start this new season in the Premier League, I’m feeling good and ready for the challenge.

“I was at Burnley last season in the Premier League, which was incredible.

“I’m going to bring my energy, determination and leadership to the team. I’ve played in Ligue 1, Serie A and now I’m playing in the Premier League, the best league in the world, so I have a lot of experience for my young age.

“I’m so excited to play at the Coventry Building Society Arena and I can’t wait for the new season."

Hull are set to complete the signing Swedish international Elliot Stroud, talkSPORT understands.

Stroud has rejected an offer from Genoa to move to the Premier League new boys from Mjallby, with a £3million deal in place.

The 24-year-old left-back featured four times for Sweden at the World Cup, and started in their round of 32 exit against France.

Hull are gearing up for their first season back in the top flight since 2017, after victory in the Championship play-off final in May.

So far, their only summer signing has seen goalkeeper Jack Butland arrive from Rangers for an undisclosed fee.

Hull were also forced to sell former no.1 Ivor Pandur and midfielder Aidon Shehu hours before the end of June, which meant that they avoided a points deduction for breach of PSR rules.

Chelsea have slapped a €50million (£42.5m) price tag on Alejandro Garnacho as they brace themselves for offers in the coming weeks, talkSPORT understands.

talkSPORT previously reported that the Blues winger was up for sale this summer, just a year after he joined the club for £40million from Manchester United.

Garnacho is attracting interest from teams in the Premier League, Italy and Saudi Arabia, with admirers at other European clubs too.

Chelsea sources say that the club are working with the Argentine to secure a permanent move, who is keen to leave after failing to be guaranteed a regular starting role.

Garnacho is yet to report for pre-season training due to interest from multiple teams, with his future to be resolved in the next fortnight.

The 22-year-old only scored one Premier League goal during his first season as a Chelsea player last term.

He featured 24 times in the top flight, but only started on 14 occasions, struggling to hold down a first-team place.

Across all competitions, he played 43 times for the Blues in total, scoring eight and assisting four goals last campaign.

Everton are reportedly keen on signing Newcastle winger Jacob Murphy, who has a year left on his current deal.

The 31-year-old signed for his boyhood club nine years ago and has spent almost his entire career on Tyneside.

Murphy is one of a number of players Everton are considering as they look to strengthen the forward line.

The Toffees are yet to make an offer for the Magpies wide man, but Sky Sports report that they are interested in his availability.

It remains to be seen whether Jack Grealish will commit to the club this summer, having joined on loan last year with the option to make the deal permanent at the end of the season for £50million.

Should Murphy leave Newcastle, it would mark yet another St James' Park departure this summer.

Anthony Gordon completed a £70m move to Barcelona in May, before Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham in a £100m deal.

Meanwhile, captain Bruno Guimaraes now also looks set to leave, having agreed terms with Arsenal after informing the club of his desire to join the Premier League champions.

Former Luton captain Tom Lockyer has completed a move to Australian side Melbourne Victory.

The 31-year-old joins on a free transfer, after leaving Bristol Rovers at the end of last season.

Lockyer made his return to football with the League Two side last season, after nearly two years out following a cardiac arrest during a Premier League match for Luton in 2023.

This was the second time the defender had collapsed on a pitch, after suffering a first incident in the 2023 Championship play-off final.

The 16-cap Wales international made 16 league appearances for Bristol Rovers last term, and welcomed his latest career move.

After joining Melbourne Victory, he said: “I am thrilled to have joined Melbourne Victory and cannot wait to get this next chapter of my career underway in such an amazing city.

“This opportunity excites me a lot, as I look to experience new things and challenge myself in a fresh environment.

"Now it is time to get to work and be ready for every battle ahead.”

Rangers have complete the signing of Cammy Devlin, following the midfielder's departure from Hearts.

The Australian has penned a two-year deal with the option of an additional 12 months, is the third significant arrival at Ibrox from Hearts this summer.

Lawrence Shankland moved prior to representing Scotland at the World Cup , while Derek McInnes has been appointed as manager.

Devlin spent five years at Tynecastle, making 171 appearances and scoring eight times.

He was part of Australia's 2026 World Cup squad, but did not feature on the pitch as they were eliminated in the round of 32.

Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Jeremy Monga from Leicester on a five-year deal.

The England Under-19 international, who turned 17 on Friday, joins for a reported fee of £10million plus add-ons.

Monga had looked set to join Arsenal, with talkSPORT reporting in May that a fee had been agreed for the teenager, only to pull out after feeling his valuation was too high, allowing City to swoop in.

The young forward played 30 times in all competitions for Leicester last term, contributing one goal and two assists as they were relegated to League One.

Monga now becomes City's fourth summer signing, following the arrivals of Elliot Anderson, Mathys Detourbet and Pierce Charles.

Upon signing, the starlet said: “When I became aware that Manchester City were interested, I knew instantly this was the right choice for me.

“For any young footballer, to become part of this amazing club is a dream come true.

“This has been the best club in England over the past 10 years. And it has also handed opportunities to players from the Academy like Phil Foden and Nico O’Reilly which shows that the pathway is there.

“It is a privilege to be here and I’m delighted to have joined.”

Harry Winks is closing in on a surprise move to Serie A side Cagliari.

The Leicester City midfielder has been strongly linked with a move away from the club since their relegation to League One was confirmed in April.

Winks, one of the Foxes’ highest earners, joined the Midlands club in 2023 in a £10million deal and played a key role in their Championship title success under Enzo Maresca.

However, he suffered fallouts with two future Leicester managers and held a frosty relationship with the club’s supporters.

Kurt Zouma has signed for Palm City, according to reports.

The former Chelsea and West Ham defender leaves UAE Pro League club Al Wasl FC without making a single appearance in five months.

Zouma now drops down to the second tier in western Asia to sign for fellow Emirati side Palm City, who compete in the UAE First Division League.

Transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano reports that the deal is all-but done.

After seeing his move from Wolves to Atletico Madrid stall, Joao Gomes has posted on social media.

The Brazilian was all set for a move to to the Spanish capital, but the plug has been pulled.

That means Gomes will be playing in the Championship next season, as it stands.

However, you would now expect Premier League teams to circle.

And he's clearly confident things will work out.

Harry Winks could be set for an instant escape from League One.

Fabrizio Romano is reporting that the former England international is on the verge of a move to Italy.

Serie A side Cagliari are in talks to take the midfielder from the King Power.

Winks is a very unpopular figure among Leicester fans and was caught in several arguments with him as the Foxes suffered back-to-back relegations.

Mohamed Salah has emerged as a top target for Sporting Kansas City, according to reports.

The Athletic believe that the MLS side are readying a very ambitious move for the Egyptian international.

Salah is a free agent having left Liverpool after a remarkable career on Merseyside.

talkSPORT understands that a move to the USA is a long shot with Saudi Arabian clubs still leading the way for the most famous practicing Muslim player in the world.

talkSPORT understands that Manchester United sources deny that Ederson's move is off.

Fabrizio Romano reported earlier this evening that it was over for the Brazilian.

However, Man United sources have now come back to talkSPORT and informed us that the deal is still on.

The midfielder is undergoing an intensive medical due to concerns over a longstanding injury.

It appears that Ederson's proposed transfer from Atalanta to Manchester United is OFF.

Fabrizio Romano is reporting that the Red Devils have cancelled the transfer.

talkSPORT reported a couple of days ago that the player would be put through an extensive medical process to determine if a long-standing knee problem was a concern.

And after a two-part medical, Man United have elected not to sign him.

Atalanta believe the player is totally fine, and he will be part of their squad for pre-season.

The Red Devils have already completed the signing of Andrey Santos from Chelsea this summer.

Coventry City have agreed a club-record fee for Aurele Amenda.

The newly promoted side are set to pay Frankfurt £17million, which blow their current record out of the water.

The 22-year-old is a centre-back with seven caps for his country.

He is at the World Cup but is yet to appear in a single game for the Swiss.

Burnley have confirmed the appointment of Nicky Hayen as their manager.

Hayen has signed a three-year deal at Turf Moor and replaces Scott Parker, who was sacked near the end of last season.

Burnley made the move for Hayen after an attempt to get Craig Bellamy collapsed.

The 45-year-old arrives from Genk, and he won the Belgian Pro League with Club Brugge.

Speaking to the club's website, he said: “I'm pleased to be joining a club with real history and supporters who care deeply about it. I know most of them won't know much about me yet, that's fair and it's on me to change it.

“What I can tell them is how my teams play. We keep the ball, we press with purpose, and we trust young players with real minutes, not just a place on the bench.

“I'm really looking forward to working with the squad in the US on the pre-season tour. The hard work starts there.”
